steps.instruction: Wash the bike, especially the fork tubes and clamps, and set up a clean bench with lint-free rags. Dirt inside this fork is the main cause of short seal and damper life.
steps.title: Wash and prep

steps.instruction: Write down the compression and rebound clicker positions (count in to the stop, then return) and how far the fork tubes stand above the top clamp on each side.
steps.title: Record settings and height

steps.instruction: Put the bike on a stand under the engine with the front wheel clear and check it is stable.
steps.title: Lift the front wheel

steps.instruction: Loosen the four axle pinch bolts at the bottom of both fork legs, then crack the axle nut loose. Do not take anything off yet; the wheel is still holding the forks in line.
steps.title: Loosen the axle
verification: Pinch bolts and axle nut loose

steps.instruction: Hold the wheel, unscrew the axle nut and slide the axle out. Lower the wheel out of the forks and lay it with the disc facing up. Pick up the two collars from the hub and keep them with the axle so they go back on the correct sides.
steps.title: Pull the front wheel
verification: Wheel out, axle and both collars bagged together

steps.instruction: Remove the two caliper bolts, slide the caliper off the disc and hang it from the frame with a strap so the hose is not stretched. Do not pull the brake lever while it is off.
steps.title: Unbolt and hang the caliper

steps.instruction: Take out the number plate bolt and lift the plate off.
steps.title: Remove the number plate

steps.instruction: Undo the fork guard (protector) bolts on each leg and take the guards off, freeing the brake hose and any sensor lead from their guides.
steps.title: Remove the fork guards

steps.instruction: Loosen the upper clamp pinch bolts on one leg. With the leg still held by the lower clamp, crack the damper assembly (fork cap) loose with the cap bolt ring wrench. Repeat on the other leg.
steps.title: Loosen the fork caps in the clamps

steps.instruction: Hold each leg, loosen its lower clamp pinch bolts and slide it down out of the clamps. Label them left and right.
steps.title: Pull both legs

steps.instruction: Clamp the leg upright in a soft-jaw vise by the axle bracket, unscrew the damper assembly from the outer tube, and pump the outer tube to drain the oil into a pan. Look at the oil: metal flakes or a grey colour mean worn bushings.
steps.title: Unscrew the cap and drain the outer oil

steps.instruction: Compress the inner tube and slip the cap bolt ring wrench in between the inner tube and the damper locknut so the damper rod is held out. Hold the locknut and unscrew the adjuster at the bottom of the leg. Leave the locknut where it is: if you remove it the damper rod can drop inside the damper and is hard to recover. Pull out the damper adjusting rod (if fitted), then the damper with its spring and spring seat.
steps.title: Remove the bottom adjuster
verification: Adjuster off, locknut still on the rod

steps.instruction: Pry the dust seal up out of the outer tube, then lift the stopper ring out of its groove with a wrapped flat screwdriver. Do not scratch the inner tube.
steps.title: Remove the dust seal and stopper ring
verification: Dust seal and stopper ring out

steps.instruction: Push the inner tube in slowly until it is just short of bottoming, then pull it out sharply. Repeat until the bushings knock the oil seal out and the tubes come apart. Slide the old seal, washer and bushings off the inner tube.
steps.title: Separate the tubes

steps.instruction: Note the compression clicker position and turn it fully out. Hold the damper with the cap bolt ring wrench and unscrew the base valve with the cap bolt wrench. Drain the damper oil.
steps.title: Remove the base valve from the damper

steps.instruction: Check the inner tube chrome for scratches and the oil lock piece for damage; light marks can be polished with 1000-grit wet paper. Roll the tube in V-blocks under a dial gauge: the bend is half the gauge swing and must not exceed 0.2 mm. Check the outer tube bore for wear or scoring. Record the bend reading.
steps.title: Inspect the tubes
verification: Inner tube bend at or under 0.2 mm

steps.instruction: Measure the fork spring free length. Under 492.0 mm it must be replaced.
steps.title: Measure the spring

steps.instruction: Check the damper for a bent rod or damage and its O-ring for wear. Check the base valve, its O-ring, bushing and spring and the bleed screw for wear or damage, clean the base valve if dirty, and check the upper spring seat face, the adjuster and its O-ring. Replace anything worn.
steps.title: Inspect the damper and valves
verification: Damper, base valve, adjuster and seats inspected

steps.instruction: Wash all parts in clean solvent, blow them dry and lay them on clean rags. No grit or lint may get into the damper.
steps.title: Clean every part

steps.instruction: Pull the damper rod all the way out. Fill the damper with Yamaha Suspension Oil S1 (216 cm³). Pump the rod slowly up and down in strokes of about 200 mm to push the air out. Do not use longer strokes; that draws air back in, and if it happens start the fill again.
steps.title: Fill the damper
verification: Damper filled and bled with short strokes

steps.instruction: With the rod fully extended, measure from the top of the damper down to the oil and set it to 145–148 mm by adding or drawing off oil. Do the same on the other damper; both must match.
steps.title: Set the damper oil level
verification: Oil level 145–148 mm in both dampers

steps.instruction: Run the locknut fully down the damper rod by hand. Pull the damper rod out to full extension, then fit the base valve and let the rod come back as you screw it in. Check the damper is still fully extended; if not, repeat the fill and level steps. Hold the damper with the ring wrench and torque the base valve to 28 N·m (21 lb-ft).
steps.title: Refit the base valve

steps.instruction: Pump the damper rod slowly through its full travel more than 10 times to spread the oil. Then, with a cloth around the damper, push it fully in and hold it while the excess oil (about 10 cm³) runs out of the hole on the base valve end. Check the damper moves smoothly with no tight spots; if not, start again from the fill.
steps.title: Purge the excess oil

steps.instruction: Cover the end of the inner tube with a plastic bag wiped with fork oil so the seal lips are not cut. Slide on, in this order: new dust seal, stopper ring, new oil seal with its numbered side facing down toward the axle, washer, and the new outer tube bushing. Grease the dust seal and oil seal lips with lithium-soap grease and oil the inner tube.
steps.title: Load the new parts onto the inner tube
verification: Parts on in the right order

steps.instruction: Fit the new inner tube bushing (piston metal) into its slot at the top of the inner tube.
steps.title: Fit the new inner tube bushing

steps.instruction: Slide the outer tube onto the inner tube. Drive the outer tube bushing and washer into the outer tube with the fork seal driver until seated.
steps.title: Join the tubes and drive in the bushing

steps.instruction: Drive the new oil seal in with the fork seal driver until the stopper ring groove is completely visible above it, then fit the stopper ring fully into its groove.
steps.title: Drive in the oil seal and stopper ring

steps.instruction: Grease the inner tube, then press the new dust seal into the top of the outer tube. Slide the tubes through their stroke; they must move smoothly. If they bind, take them apart again and find out why.
steps.title: Fit the dust seal

steps.instruction: Measure from the bottom of the damper body to the bottom of the locknut on the rod. It must be 16 mm or more; turn the locknut to get it there.
steps.title: Check the locknut position on the damper rod

steps.instruction: Put the upper spring seat on with its larger diameter toward the spring, slide the spring onto the damper, and lower the damper slowly into the inner tube until it rests on the bottom. Do not let it drop; it can damage the tube.
steps.title: Fit the spring and damper
verification: Spring seat the right way round

steps.instruction: Turn the rebound clicker fully out (note where it was). Compress the inner tube and hold the damper rod out with the ring wrench between the tube and the locknut. Fit the damper adjusting rod (if fitted), a new copper washer and the adjuster, finger tight against the locknut. Measure the gap between adjuster and locknut: it must be 0.5–1.0 mm. Then hold the locknut and torque the adjuster to it at 29 N·m (21 lb-ft).
steps.title: Fit the adjuster to the damper rod
verification: Adjuster on the locknut at 29 N·m (21 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Put medium threadlocker on the adjuster threads, remove the ring wrench and screw the adjuster into the bottom of the inner tube. Torque it to 55 N·m (41 lb-ft).
steps.title: Screw the adjuster into the inner tube

steps.instruction: Fill the leg with 290 cm³ of Yamaha Suspension Oil S1 (the adjustment range is 260–365 cm³). Use the same amount on both legs.
steps.title: Fill the outer chamber

steps.instruction: Screw the damper assembly (fork cap) into the outer tube by hand; it gets its final torque once the leg is in the clamps. Refit the protector guide.
steps.title: Refit the fork cap

steps.instruction: Slide each leg up through the clamps to the height you recorded (stock is 5 mm of tube above the top clamp). Snug the lower pinch bolts just enough to hold the leg.
steps.title: Put the legs back in the clamps
verification: Both legs at the same height (5 mm stock)

steps.instruction: Torque each damper assembly (fork cap) to 30 N·m (22 lb-ft) with the cap bolt ring wrench.
steps.title: Torque the fork caps

steps.instruction: Recheck the heights, then tighten the upper pinch bolts to 21 N·m (15 lb-ft) and the lower pinch bolts to 21 N·m (15 lb-ft). Do not overtighten the lower clamp; that squeezes the tube and makes the fork stick.
steps.title: Torque the clamp pinch bolts

steps.instruction: Refit the guards with the brake hose and any sensor lead in their guides and tighten the guard bolts to 5 N·m (3.7 lb-ft) (brake hose holder bolt 9 N·m (6.6 lb-ft)).
steps.title: Refit the fork guards

steps.instruction: Refit the number plate (bolt 7 N·m (5.2 lb-ft)).
steps.title: Refit the number plate

steps.instruction: Unhook the caliper and bolt it back onto the left fork leg, torquing its two bolts to 28 N·m (21 lb-ft). Check the pads are still seated and spread enough for the disc.
steps.title: Bolt the caliper back on

steps.instruction: Grease the axle lightly with lithium-soap grease. Fit the collars to the hub on their own sides, lift the wheel into the forks with the disc sliding between the brake pads, and push the axle through from the side it came out.
steps.title: Lift the front wheel into the forks

steps.instruction: Fit the axle nut and run it down. Before the final pull, take the bike off the stand or push hard on the bars a few times so the forks settle and slide freely on the axle. Then torque the axle nut to 115 N·m (85 lb-ft).
steps.title: Torque the axle nut

steps.instruction: Tighten the four axle pinch bolts to 21 N·m (15 lb-ft), going back and forth between the two bolts on each leg so the clamp closes evenly.
steps.title: Tighten the axle pinch bolts
verification: All four pinch bolts at 21 N·m (15 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Squeeze the front brake lever several times until it is firm, then spin the wheel. It should turn freely with only light pad drag and stop hard when you pull the lever.
steps.title: Pump up the front brake
verification: Wheel spins freely and brakes properly

steps.instruction: Turn the rebound and compression clickers in until they stop gently, then back out to your recorded positions. With the front wheel off the ground, take out the bleed screw on top of each fork leg to release the internal pressure, then refit it at 1.3 N·m (0.95 lb-ft).
steps.title: Restore clickers and bleed air
verification: Pressure released, bleed screws at 1.3 N·m (0.95 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Off the stand, push the front down hard several times: the fork should move smoothly and quietly with no oil on the tubes. Recheck after the first ride for seal leaks.
steps.title: Final check

required_tools.name: Cap bolt ring wrench (holds the damper/locknut)
Cap bolt wrench for the base valve
Ruler or fork oil level gauge reading from the top of the damper
Yamaha Suspension Oil S1 fork oil
Plastic bag or thin film to protect the new seal lips
Flat-blade screwdriver (wrapped) for the stopper ring

steps.instruction: Wash the bike, especially the fork tubes and clamps, and set up a clean bench with lint-free rags. Dirt inside this fork is the main cause of short seal and damper life.
steps.title: Wash and prep

steps.instruction: Write down the compression and rebound clicker positions (count in to the stop, then return) and how far the fork tubes stand above the top clamp on each side.
steps.title: Record settings and height

steps.instruction: Put the bike on a stand under the engine with the front wheel clear and check it is stable.
steps.title: Lift the front wheel

steps.instruction: Loosen the four axle pinch bolts at the bottom of both fork legs, then crack the axle nut loose. Do not take anything off yet; the wheel is still holding the forks in line.
steps.title: Loosen the axle
verification: Pinch bolts and axle nut loose

steps.instruction: Hold the wheel, unscrew the axle nut and slide the axle out. Lower the wheel out of the forks and lay it with the disc facing up. Pick up the two collars from the hub and keep them with the axle so they go back on the correct sides.
steps.title: Pull the front wheel
verification: Wheel out, axle and both collars bagged together

steps.instruction: Remove the two caliper bolts, slide the caliper off the disc and hang it from the frame with a strap so the hose is not stretched. Do not pull the brake lever while it is off.
steps.title: Unbolt and hang the caliper

steps.instruction: Take out the number plate bolt and lift the plate off.
steps.title: Remove the number plate

steps.instruction: Undo the fork guard (protector) bolts on each leg and take the guards off, freeing the brake hose and any sensor lead from their guides.
steps.title: Remove the fork guards

steps.instruction: Loosen the upper clamp pinch bolts on one leg. With the leg still held by the lower clamp, crack the damper assembly (fork cap) loose with the cap bolt ring wrench. Repeat on the other leg.
steps.title: Loosen the fork caps in the clamps

steps.instruction: Hold each leg, loosen its lower clamp pinch bolts and slide it down out of the clamps. Label them left and right.
steps.title: Pull both legs

steps.instruction: Clamp the leg upright in a soft-jaw vise by the axle bracket, unscrew the damper assembly from the outer tube, and pump the outer tube to drain the oil into a pan. Look at the oil: metal flakes or a grey colour mean worn bushings.
steps.title: Unscrew the cap and drain the outer oil

steps.instruction: Compress the inner tube and slip the cap bolt ring wrench in between the inner tube and the damper locknut so the damper rod is held out. Hold the locknut and unscrew the adjuster at the bottom of the leg. Leave the locknut where it is: if you remove it the damper rod can drop inside the damper and is hard to recover. Pull out the damper adjusting rod (if fitted), then the damper with its spring and spring seat.
steps.title: Remove the bottom adjuster
verification: Adjuster off, locknut still on the rod

steps.instruction: Pry the dust seal up out of the outer tube, then lift the stopper ring out of its groove with a wrapped flat screwdriver. Do not scratch the inner tube. Slide the scraper off too.
steps.title: Remove the dust seal and stopper ring
verification: Dust seal and stopper ring out

steps.instruction: Push the inner tube in slowly until it is just short of bottoming, then pull it out sharply. Repeat until the bushings knock the oil seal out and the tubes come apart. Slide the old seal, washer and bushings off the inner tube.
steps.title: Separate the tubes

steps.instruction: Note the compression clicker position and turn it fully out (remove the adjuster knob screw and knob first). Hold the damper with the cap bolt ring wrench and unscrew the base valve with the cap bolt wrench. Drain the damper oil.
steps.title: Remove the base valve from the damper

steps.instruction: Check the inner tube chrome for scratches and the oil lock piece for damage; light marks can be polished with 1000-grit wet paper. Roll the tube in V-blocks under a dial gauge: the bend is half the gauge swing and must not exceed 0.2 mm. Check the outer tube bore for wear or scoring. Record the bend reading.
steps.title: Inspect the tubes
verification: Inner tube bend at or under 0.2 mm

steps.instruction: Measure the fork spring free length. Under 492.0 mm it must be replaced.
steps.title: Measure the spring

steps.instruction: Check the damper for a bent rod or damage and its O-ring for wear. Check the base valve, its O-ring, bushing and spring and the bleed screw for wear or damage, clean the base valve if dirty, and check the upper spring seat face, the adjuster and its O-ring and the scraper. Replace anything worn.
steps.title: Inspect the damper and valves
verification: Damper, base valve, adjuster and seats inspected

steps.instruction: Wash all parts in clean solvent, blow them dry and lay them on clean rags. No grit or lint may get into the damper.
steps.title: Clean every part

steps.instruction: Pull the damper rod all the way out. Fill the damper with Yamaha Suspension Oil S1 (219 cm³). Pump the rod slowly up and down in strokes of about 200 mm to push the air out. Do not use longer strokes; that draws air back in, and if it happens start the fill again.
steps.title: Fill the damper
verification: Damper filled and bled with short strokes

steps.instruction: With the rod fully extended, measure from the top of the damper down to the oil and set it to 143–146 mm by adding or drawing off oil. Do the same on the other damper; both must match.
steps.title: Set the damper oil level
verification: Oil level 143–146 mm in both dampers

steps.instruction: Run the locknut fully down the damper rod by hand. Pull the damper rod out to full extension, then fit the base valve and let the rod come back as you screw it in. Check the damper is still fully extended; if not, repeat the fill and level steps. Hold the damper with the ring wrench and torque the base valve to 28 N·m (21 lb-ft), then fit the adjuster knob and its screw at 0.6 N·m (0.44 lb-ft).
steps.title: Refit the base valve

steps.instruction: Pump the damper rod slowly through its full travel more than 10 times to spread the oil. Then, with a cloth around the damper, push it fully in and hold it while the excess oil (about 10 cm³) runs out of the hole on the base valve end. Check the damper moves smoothly with no tight spots; if not, start again from the fill.
steps.title: Purge the excess oil

steps.instruction: Cover the end of the inner tube with a plastic bag wiped with fork oil so the seal lips are not cut. Slide on, in this order: new dust seal, scraper, stopper ring, new oil seal with its numbered side facing down toward the axle, washer, and the new outer tube bushing. Grease the dust seal and oil seal lips with lithium-soap grease and oil the inner tube.
steps.title: Load the new parts onto the inner tube
verification: Parts on in the right order

steps.instruction: Fit the new inner tube bushing (piston metal) into its slot at the top of the inner tube.
steps.title: Fit the new inner tube bushing

steps.instruction: Slide the outer tube onto the inner tube. Drive the outer tube bushing and washer into the outer tube with the fork seal driver until seated.
steps.title: Join the tubes and drive in the bushing

steps.instruction: Drive the new oil seal in with the fork seal driver until the stopper ring groove is completely visible above it, then fit the stopper ring fully into its groove.
steps.title: Drive in the oil seal and stopper ring

steps.instruction: Grease the inner tube, then press the scraper and new dust seal into the top of the outer tube. Slide the tubes through their stroke; they must move smoothly. If they bind, take them apart again and find out why.
steps.title: Fit the dust seal

steps.instruction: Measure from the bottom of the damper body to the bottom of the locknut on the rod. It must be 16 mm or more; turn the locknut to get it there.
steps.title: Check the locknut position on the damper rod

steps.instruction: Put the upper spring seat on with its larger diameter toward the spring, slide the spring onto the damper, and lower the damper slowly into the inner tube until it rests on the bottom. Do not let it drop; it can damage the tube.
steps.title: Fit the spring and damper
verification: Spring seat the right way round

steps.instruction: Turn the rebound clicker fully out (note where it was). Compress the inner tube and hold the damper rod out with the ring wrench between the tube and the locknut. Fit the damper adjusting rod (if fitted), a new copper washer and the adjuster, finger tight against the locknut. Measure the gap between adjuster and locknut: it must be 0.5–1.0 mm. Then hold the locknut and torque the adjuster to it at 29 N·m (21 lb-ft).
steps.title: Fit the adjuster to the damper rod
verification: Adjuster on the locknut at 29 N·m (21 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Put medium threadlocker on the adjuster threads, remove the ring wrench and screw the adjuster into the bottom of the inner tube. Torque it to 55 N·m (41 lb-ft).
steps.title: Screw the adjuster into the inner tube

steps.instruction: Fill the leg with 280 cm³ of Yamaha Suspension Oil S1 (the adjustment range is 260–370 cm³). Use the same amount on both legs.
steps.title: Fill the outer chamber

steps.instruction: Screw the damper assembly (fork cap) into the outer tube by hand; it gets its final torque once the leg is in the clamps. Refit the protector guide.
steps.title: Refit the fork cap

steps.instruction: Slide each leg up through the clamps to the height you recorded (stock is 8 mm of tube above the top clamp). Snug the lower pinch bolts just enough to hold the leg.
steps.title: Put the legs back in the clamps
verification: Both legs at the same height (8 mm stock)

steps.instruction: Torque each damper assembly (fork cap) to 30 N·m (22 lb-ft) with the cap bolt ring wrench.
steps.title: Torque the fork caps

steps.instruction: Recheck the heights, then tighten the upper pinch bolts to 21 N·m (15 lb-ft) and the lower pinch bolts to 21 N·m (15 lb-ft). Do not overtighten the lower clamp; that squeezes the tube and makes the fork stick.
steps.title: Torque the clamp pinch bolts

steps.instruction: Refit the guards with the brake hose and any sensor lead in their guides and tighten the guard bolts to 7 N·m (5.2 lb-ft) (brake hose holder bolt 9 N·m (6.6 lb-ft)).
steps.title: Refit the fork guards

steps.instruction: Refit the number plate (bolt 7 N·m (5.2 lb-ft)).
steps.title: Refit the number plate

steps.instruction: Unhook the caliper and bolt it back onto the left fork leg, torquing its two bolts to 28 N·m (21 lb-ft). Check the pads are still seated and spread enough for the disc.
steps.title: Bolt the caliper back on

steps.instruction: Grease the axle lightly with lithium-soap grease. Fit the collars to the hub on their own sides, lift the wheel into the forks with the disc sliding between the brake pads, and push the axle through from the side it came out.
steps.title: Lift the front wheel into the forks

steps.instruction: Fit the axle nut and run it down. Before the final pull, take the bike off the stand or push hard on the bars a few times so the forks settle and slide freely on the axle. Then torque the axle nut to 115 N·m (85 lb-ft).
steps.title: Torque the axle nut

steps.instruction: Tighten the four axle pinch bolts to 21 N·m (15 lb-ft), going back and forth between the two bolts on each leg so the clamp closes evenly.
steps.title: Tighten the axle pinch bolts
verification: All four pinch bolts at 21 N·m (15 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Squeeze the front brake lever several times until it is firm, then spin the wheel. It should turn freely with only light pad drag and stop hard when you pull the lever.
steps.title: Pump up the front brake
verification: Wheel spins freely and brakes properly

steps.instruction: Turn the rebound and compression clickers in until they stop gently, then back out to your recorded positions. With the front wheel off the ground, take out the bleed screw on top of each fork leg to release the internal pressure, then refit it at 1.3 N·m (0.95 lb-ft).
steps.title: Restore clickers and bleed air
verification: Pressure released, bleed screws at 1.3 N·m (0.95 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Off the stand, push the front down hard several times: the fork should move smoothly and quietly with no oil on the tubes. Recheck after the first ride for seal leaks.
steps.title: Final check

title: Full fork service: seals, bushings, oil and damper bleed

completeness: Takes both fork legs off the bike, strips them, inspects the tubes, spring, damper and base valve, renews the oil seal, dust seal, both bushings and copper washer, refills and bleeds the closed damper, sets its oil level and the outer-chamber oil, and refits the legs at the correct height with clickers restored; internal damper valving is not altered.
critical_stop_conditions: Inner tube bent more than 0.2 mm (half the dial reading): replace the tube, never straighten it.
Inner tube chrome pitted or scored deeper than fine wet sanding can remove, or the oil lock piece damaged: replace the tube.
Fork spring shorter than 492.0 mm: replace it.
Damper rod bent or the damper leaks: replace the damper assembly.
Oil levels in the two legs different: correct before riding; uneven legs make the bike unstable.
Front brake not firm after refit: do not ride.
entry_state: Complete bike, cold, on a stand under the engine.
excluded: Damper cartridge internal rebuild beyond the base valve and oil
exit_state: Both fork legs serviced with new seals, bushings and oil, refitted at the stock height with all clamp, axle and caliper torques set and clickers restored; ready to ride.
prerequisites: Bike washed, especially the fork tubes and clamps.
Clicker positions and fork height recorded.
Clean bench: the damper is very sensitive to dirt.

title: Full fork service: seals, bushings, oil and damper bleed

completeness: Takes the shock out, removes the spring, inspects the shock body, renews the lower eye bearing and upper eye bushing with their seals, refits the spring at your recorded preload and reinstalls the shock with the linkage torqued; the nitrogen-charged damper is not opened, so damper oil, seals, valving and gas recharge are not covered.
critical_stop_conditions: Shock rod bent, scored or leaking oil or gas: the shock must be replaced or rebuilt by a suspension shop.
Never heat, puncture or clamp the damper body, and never try to open it: it holds high-pressure nitrogen.
Shock eye bore scored or out of round: stop, the shock body is damaged.
Spring cracked or worn through its coating at the guides: replace it.
Shock does not return fully or knocks after refit: do not ride.
entry_state: Complete bike, cold, on a stand under the engine with the rear wheel clear.
excluded: Damper internals: oil, seal head, piston, valving and nitrogen recharge (the damper is sealed and is not opened)
Linkage and swingarm needle bearings (see the linkage guide)
Changing to a different spring rate
exit_state: Shock refitted with inspected spring and new eye bearing/bushing and seals, preload restored, linkage torqued; ready to ride. Damper internals untouched.
prerequisites: Bike washed; seat, side covers, shrouds and fuel tank off for access to the top shock bolt.
Record the shock clicker positions and measure the spring installed length before you touch the adjuster.

steps.instruction: Wash the bike, especially around the shock and linkage, and let it dry.
steps.title: Wash and prep

steps.instruction: Take off the seat, both side covers, both shrouds and the fuel tank so you can reach the top shock bolt. Bag each set of fasteners separately.
steps.title: Remove the seat, side covers, shrouds and tank

steps.instruction: Put the bike on a stand under the engine with the rear wheel clear. Support the swingarm with a block so it cannot drop when the shock comes out.
steps.title: Lift the rear wheel

steps.instruction: Count the rebound and both compression clicker positions back to the stop and write them down, then reset them. Measure the spring installed length (between the spring seats) and write it down so you can restore the same preload.
steps.title: Record shock settings and spring length

steps.instruction: Hold the swingarm and pull the shock lower bolt out of the relay arm.
steps.title: Remove the shock lower bolt

steps.instruction: Remove the upper bolt nut and bolt and lift the shock out downward and backward between the linkage and the frame. Keep it upright.
steps.title: Remove the shock upper bolt and shock

steps.instruction: Clamp the shock body lightly in a soft-jaw vise. Loosen the locknut, back the adjusting nut off until the spring is free, then remove the lower spring guide, upper spring guide and spring. Do not turn the shock shaft or touch the gas valve.
steps.title: Take the spring off

steps.instruction: Wash the bike, especially the fork tubes and clamps, and set up a clean bench with lint-free rags. Dirt inside this fork is the main cause of short seal and damper life.
steps.title: Wash and prep

steps.instruction: Write down the compression and rebound clicker positions (count in to the stop, then return) and how far the fork tubes stand above the top clamp on each side.
steps.title: Record settings and height

steps.instruction: Put the bike on a stand under the engine with the front wheel clear and check it is stable.
steps.title: Lift the front wheel

steps.instruction: Undo the speed sensor bracket bolt on the left fork leg and lift the sensor away from the wheel without pulling on its lead. Tape it to the fork guard so it hangs clear. Keep magnetic tools away from the sensor and its rotor on the wheel.
steps.title: Unbolt the speed sensor
verification: Sensor hanging free, lead not stretched

steps.instruction: Loosen the four axle pinch bolts at the bottom of both fork legs, then crack the axle nut loose. Do not take anything off yet; the wheel is still holding the forks in line.
steps.title: Loosen the axle
verification: Pinch bolts and axle nut loose

steps.instruction: Hold the wheel, unscrew the axle nut and slide the axle out. Lower the wheel out of the forks and lay it with the disc facing up. Pick up the two collars from the hub and keep them with the axle so they go back on the correct sides.
steps.title: Pull the front wheel
verification: Wheel out, axle and both collars bagged together

steps.instruction: Remove the two caliper bolts, slide the caliper off the disc and hang it from the frame with a strap so the hose is not stretched. Do not pull the brake lever while it is off.
steps.title: Unbolt and hang the caliper

steps.instruction: Take the headlight body off so you can reach the top of the fork legs, leaving it hanging on its wiring with no strain.
steps.title: Move the headlight out of the way
verification: Headlight clear of the fork caps

steps.instruction: Undo the fork guard (protector) bolts on each leg and take the guards off, freeing the brake hose and any sensor lead from their guides.
steps.title: Remove the fork guards

steps.instruction: Loosen the upper clamp pinch bolts on one leg. With the leg still held by the lower clamp, crack the damper assembly (fork cap) loose with the cap bolt ring wrench. Repeat on the other leg.
steps.title: Loosen the fork caps in the clamps

steps.instruction: Hold each leg, loosen its lower clamp pinch bolts and slide it down out of the clamps. Label them left and right.
steps.title: Pull both legs

steps.instruction: Clamp the leg upright in a soft-jaw vise by the axle bracket, unscrew the damper assembly from the outer tube, and pump the outer tube to drain the oil into a pan. Look at the oil: metal flakes or a grey colour mean worn bushings.
steps.title: Unscrew the cap and drain the outer oil

steps.instruction: Compress the inner tube and slip the cap bolt ring wrench in between the inner tube and the damper locknut so the damper rod is held out. Hold the locknut and unscrew the adjuster at the bottom of the leg. Leave the locknut where it is: if you remove it the damper rod can drop inside the damper and is hard to recover. Pull out the damper adjusting rod (if fitted), then the damper with its spring and spring seat.
steps.title: Remove the bottom adjuster
verification: Adjuster off, locknut still on the rod

steps.instruction: Pry the dust seal up out of the outer tube, then lift the stopper ring out of its groove with a wrapped flat screwdriver. Do not scratch the inner tube.
steps.title: Remove the dust seal and stopper ring
verification: Dust seal and stopper ring out

steps.instruction: Push the inner tube in slowly until it is just short of bottoming, then pull it out sharply. Repeat until the bushings knock the oil seal out and the tubes come apart. Slide the old seal, washer and bushings off the inner tube.
steps.title: Separate the tubes

steps.instruction: Note the compression clicker position and turn it fully out. Hold the damper with the cap bolt ring wrench and unscrew the base valve with the cap bolt wrench. Drain the damper oil.
steps.title: Remove the base valve from the damper

steps.instruction: Check the inner tube chrome for scratches and the oil lock piece for damage; light marks can be polished with 1000-grit wet paper. Roll the tube in V-blocks under a dial gauge: the bend is half the gauge swing and must not exceed 0.2 mm. Check the outer tube bore for wear or scoring. Record the bend reading.
steps.title: Inspect the tubes
verification: Inner tube bend at or under 0.2 mm

steps.instruction: Measure the fork spring free length. Under 492.0 mm it must be replaced.
steps.title: Measure the spring

steps.instruction: Check the damper for a bent rod or damage and its O-ring for wear. Check the base valve, its O-ring, bushing and spring and the bleed screw for wear or damage, clean the base valve if dirty, and check the upper spring seat face, the adjuster and its O-ring. Replace anything worn.
steps.title: Inspect the damper and valves
verification: Damper, base valve, adjuster and seats inspected

steps.instruction: Wash all parts in clean solvent, blow them dry and lay them on clean rags. No grit or lint may get into the damper.
steps.title: Clean every part

steps.instruction: Pull the damper rod all the way out. Fill the damper with Yamaha Suspension Oil S1 (216 cm³). Pump the rod slowly up and down in strokes of about 200 mm to push the air out. Do not use longer strokes; that draws air back in, and if it happens start the fill again.
steps.title: Fill the damper
verification: Damper filled and bled with short strokes

steps.instruction: With the rod fully extended, measure from the top of the damper down to the oil and set it to 145–148 mm by adding or drawing off oil. Do the same on the other damper; both must match.
steps.title: Set the damper oil level
verification: Oil level 145–148 mm in both dampers

steps.instruction: Run the locknut fully down the damper rod by hand. Pull the damper rod out to full extension, then fit the base valve and let the rod come back as you screw it in. Check the damper is still fully extended; if not, repeat the fill and level steps. Hold the damper with the ring wrench and torque the base valve to 28 N·m (21 lb-ft).
steps.title: Refit the base valve

steps.instruction: Pump the damper rod slowly through its full travel more than 10 times to spread the oil. Then, with a cloth around the damper, push it fully in and hold it while the excess oil (about 10 cm³) runs out of the hole on the base valve end. Check the damper moves smoothly with no tight spots; if not, start again from the fill.
steps.title: Purge the excess oil

steps.instruction: Cover the end of the inner tube with a plastic bag wiped with fork oil so the seal lips are not cut. Slide on, in this order: new dust seal, stopper ring, new oil seal with its numbered side facing down toward the axle, washer, and the new outer tube bushing. Grease the dust seal and oil seal lips with lithium-soap grease and oil the inner tube.
steps.title: Load the new parts onto the inner tube
verification: Parts on in the right order

steps.instruction: Fit the new inner tube bushing (piston metal) into its slot at the top of the inner tube.
steps.title: Fit the new inner tube bushing

steps.instruction: Slide the outer tube onto the inner tube. Drive the outer tube bushing and washer into the outer tube with the fork seal driver until seated.
steps.title: Join the tubes and drive in the bushing

steps.instruction: Drive the new oil seal in with the fork seal driver until the stopper ring groove is completely visible above it, then fit the stopper ring fully into its groove.
steps.title: Drive in the oil seal and stopper ring

steps.instruction: Grease the inner tube, then press the new dust seal into the top of the outer tube. Slide the tubes through their stroke; they must move smoothly. If they bind, take them apart again and find out why.
steps.title: Fit the dust seal

steps.instruction: Measure from the bottom of the damper body to the bottom of the locknut on the rod. It must be 16 mm or more; turn the locknut to get it there.
steps.title: Check the locknut position on the damper rod

steps.instruction: Put the upper spring seat on with its larger diameter toward the spring, slide the spring onto the damper, and lower the damper slowly into the inner tube until it rests on the bottom. Do not let it drop; it can damage the tube.
steps.title: Fit the spring and damper
verification: Spring seat the right way round

steps.instruction: Turn the rebound clicker fully out (note where it was). Compress the inner tube and hold the damper rod out with the ring wrench between the tube and the locknut. Fit the damper adjusting rod (if fitted), a new copper washer and the adjuster, finger tight against the locknut. Measure the gap between adjuster and locknut: it must be 0.5–1.0 mm. Then hold the locknut and torque the adjuster to it at 29 N·m (21 lb-ft).
steps.title: Fit the adjuster to the damper rod
verification: Adjuster on the locknut at 29 N·m (21 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Put medium threadlocker on the adjuster threads, remove the ring wrench and screw the adjuster into the bottom of the inner tube. Torque it to 55 N·m (41 lb-ft).
steps.title: Screw the adjuster into the inner tube

steps.instruction: Fill the leg with 290 cm³ of Yamaha Suspension Oil S1 (the adjustment range is 260–365 cm³). Use the same amount on both legs.
steps.title: Fill the outer chamber

steps.instruction: Screw the damper assembly (fork cap) into the outer tube by hand; it gets its final torque once the leg is in the clamps. Refit the protector guide.
steps.title: Refit the fork cap

steps.instruction: Slide each leg up through the clamps to the height you recorded (stock is 5 mm of tube above the top clamp). Snug the lower pinch bolts just enough to hold the leg.
steps.title: Put the legs back in the clamps
verification: Both legs at the same height (5 mm stock)

steps.instruction: Torque each damper assembly (fork cap) to 30 N·m (22 lb-ft) with the cap bolt ring wrench.
steps.title: Torque the fork caps

steps.instruction: Recheck the heights, then tighten the upper pinch bolts to 21 N·m (15 lb-ft) and the lower pinch bolts to 21 N·m (15 lb-ft). Do not overtighten the lower clamp; that squeezes the tube and makes the fork stick.
steps.title: Torque the clamp pinch bolts

steps.instruction: Refit the guards with the brake hose and any sensor lead in their guides and tighten the guard bolts to 5 N·m (3.7 lb-ft).
steps.title: Refit the fork guards

steps.instruction: Refit the headlight body (7 N·m (5.2 lb-ft)) and check the light works.
steps.title: Refit the headlight

steps.instruction: Unhook the caliper and bolt it back onto the left fork leg, torquing its two bolts to 28 N·m (21 lb-ft). Check the pads are still seated and spread enough for the disc.
steps.title: Bolt the caliper back on

steps.instruction: Grease the axle lightly with lithium-soap grease. Fit the collars to the hub on their own sides, lift the wheel into the forks with the disc sliding between the brake pads, and push the axle through from the side it came out.
steps.title: Lift the front wheel into the forks

steps.instruction: Put the speed sensor back on the left leg with its bracket, keeping the lead in its original routing. Tighten the bolt to 7 N·m (5.2 lb-ft). Check nothing magnetic or metallic is stuck to the sensor face.
steps.title: Refit the speed sensor

steps.instruction: Fit the axle nut and run it down. Before the final pull, take the bike off the stand or push hard on the bars a few times so the forks settle and slide freely on the axle. Then torque the axle nut to 115 N·m (85 lb-ft).
steps.title: Torque the axle nut

steps.instruction: Tighten the four axle pinch bolts to 21 N·m (15 lb-ft), going back and forth between the two bolts on each leg so the clamp closes evenly.
steps.title: Tighten the axle pinch bolts
verification: All four pinch bolts at 21 N·m (15 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Squeeze the front brake lever several times until it is firm, then spin the wheel. It should turn freely with only light pad drag and stop hard when you pull the lever.
steps.title: Pump up the front brake
verification: Wheel spins freely and brakes properly

steps.instruction: Turn the rebound and compression clickers in until they stop gently, then back out to your recorded positions. With the front wheel off the ground, take out the bleed screw on top of each fork leg to release the internal pressure, then refit it at 1.3 N·m (0.95 lb-ft).
steps.title: Restore clickers and bleed air
verification: Pressure released, bleed screws at 1.3 N·m (0.95 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Off the stand, push the front down hard several times: the fork should move smoothly and quietly with no oil on the tubes. Recheck after the first ride for seal leaks.
steps.title: Final check

steps.instruction: Check the inner tube chrome for scratches and the oil lock piece for damage; light marks can be polished with 1000-grit wet paper. Roll the tube in V-blocks under a dial gauge: the bend is half the gauge swing and must not exceed 0.2 mm. Check the outer tube bore for wear or scoring. Record the bend reading.
steps.title: Inspect the tubes
verification: Inner tube bend at or under 0.2 mm

steps.instruction: Measure the fork spring free length. Under 492.0 mm it must be replaced.
steps.title: Measure the spring

steps.instruction: Check the damper for a bent rod or damage and its O-ring for wear. Check the base valve, its O-ring, bushing and spring and the bleed screw for wear or damage, clean the base valve if dirty, and check the upper spring seat face, the adjuster and its O-ring and the scraper. Replace anything worn.
steps.title: Inspect the damper and valves
verification: Damper, base valve, adjuster and seats inspected

steps.instruction: Wash all parts in clean solvent, blow them dry and lay them on clean rags. No grit or lint may get into the damper.
steps.title: Clean every part

steps.instruction: Pull the damper rod all the way out. Fill the damper with Yamaha Suspension Oil S1 (216 cm³). Pump the rod slowly up and down in strokes of about 200 mm to push the air out. Do not use longer strokes; that draws air back in, and if it happens start the fill again.

verification: Damper filled and bled with short strokes

steps.instruction: With the rod fully extended, measure from the top of the damper down to the oil and set it to 145–148 mm by adding or drawing off oil. Do the same on the other damper; both must match.
steps.title: Set the damper oil level
verification: Oil level 145–148 mm in both dampers

steps.instruction: Run the locknut fully down the damper rod by hand. Pull the damper rod out to full extension, then fit the base valve and let the rod come back as you screw it in. Check the damper is still fully extended; if not, repeat the fill and level steps. Hold the damper with the ring wrench and torque the base valve to 28 N·m (21 lb-ft).
steps.title: Refit the base valve

steps.instruction: Pump the damper rod slowly through its full travel more than 10 times to spread the oil. Then, with a cloth around the damper, push it fully in and hold it while the excess oil (about 10 cm³) runs out of the hole on the base valve end. Check the damper moves smoothly with no tight spots; if not, start again from the fill.
steps.title: Purge the excess oil

steps.instruction: Cover the end of the inner tube with a plastic bag wiped with fork oil so the seal lips are not cut. Slide on, in this order: new dust seal, scraper, stopper ring, new oil seal with its numbered side facing down toward the axle, washer, and the new outer tube bushing. Grease the dust seal and oil seal lips with lithium-soap grease and oil the inner tube.
steps.title: Load the new parts onto the inner tube
verification: Parts on in the right order

steps.instruction: Fit the new inner tube bushing (piston metal) into its slot at the top of the inner tube.
steps.title: Fit the new inner tube bushing

steps.instruction: Slide the outer tube onto the inner tube. Drive the outer tube bushing and washer into the outer tube with the fork seal driver until seated.
steps.title: Join the tubes and drive in the bushing

steps.instruction: Drive the new oil seal in with the fork seal driver until the stopper ring groove is completely visible above it, then fit the stopper ring fully into its groove.
steps.title: Drive in the oil seal and stopper ring

steps.instruction: Grease the inner tube, then press the scraper and new dust seal into the top of the outer tube. Slide the tubes through their stroke; they must move smoothly. If they bind, take them apart again and find out why.
steps.title: Fit the dust seal

steps.instruction: Measure from the bottom of the damper body to the bottom of the locknut on the rod. It must be 16 mm or more; turn the locknut to get it there.
steps.title: Check the locknut position on the damper rod

steps.instruction: Put the upper spring seat on with its larger diameter toward the spring, slide the spring onto the damper, and lower the damper slowly into the inner tube until it rests on the bottom. Do not let it drop; it can damage the tube.
steps.title: Fit the spring and damper
verification: Spring seat the right way round

steps.instruction: Turn the rebound clicker fully out (note where it was). Compress the inner tube and hold the damper rod out with the ring wrench between the tube and the locknut. Fit the damper adjusting rod (if fitted), a new copper washer and the adjuster, finger tight against the locknut. Measure the gap between adjuster and locknut: it must be 0.5–1.0 mm. Then hold the locknut and torque the adjuster to it at 29 N·m (21 lb-ft).
steps.title: Fit the adjuster to the damper rod
verification: Adjuster on the locknut at 29 N·m (21 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Put medium threadlocker on the adjuster threads, remove the ring wrench and screw the adjuster into the bottom of the inner tube. Torque it to 55 N·m (41 lb-ft).

steps.instruction: Fill the leg with 285 cm³ of Yamaha Suspension Oil S1 (the adjustment range is 260–365 cm³). Use the same amount on both legs.
steps.title: Fill the outer chamber

steps.instruction: Screw the damper assembly (fork cap) into the outer tube by hand; it gets its final torque once the leg is in the clamps. Refit the protector guide.
steps.title: Refit the fork cap

steps.instruction: Slide each leg up through the clamps to the height you recorded (stock is 5 mm of tube above the top clamp). Snug the lower pinch bolts just enough to hold the leg.
steps.title: Put the legs back in the clamps
verification: Both legs at the same height (5 mm stock)

steps.instruction: Torque each damper assembly (fork cap) to 30 N·m (22 lb-ft) with the cap bolt ring wrench.
steps.title: Torque the fork caps

steps.instruction: Recheck the heights, then tighten the upper pinch bolts to 21 N·m (15 lb-ft) and the lower pinch bolts to 21 N·m (15 lb-ft). Do not overtighten the lower clamp; that squeezes the tube and makes the fork stick.
steps.title: Torque the clamp pinch bolts

steps.instruction: Refit the guards with the brake hose and any sensor lead in their guides and tighten the guard bolts to 5 N·m (3.7 lb-ft).
steps.title: Refit the fork guards

steps.instruction: Refit the headlight body (7 N·m (5.2 lb-ft)) and check the light works.
steps.title: Refit the headlight

steps.instruction: Unhook the caliper and bolt it back onto the left fork leg, torquing its two bolts to 28 N·m (21 lb-ft). Check the pads are still seated and spread enough for the disc.
steps.title: Bolt the caliper back on

steps.instruction: Grease the axle lightly with lithium-soap grease. Fit the collars to the hub on their own sides, lift the wheel into the forks with the disc sliding between the brake pads, and push the axle through from the side it came out.
steps.title: Lift the front wheel into the forks

steps.instruction: Put the speed sensor back on the left leg with its bracket, keeping the lead in its original routing. Tighten the bolt to 7 N·m (5.2 lb-ft). Check nothing magnetic or metallic is stuck to the sensor face.

steps.instruction: Fit the axle nut and run it down. Before the final pull, take the bike off the stand or push hard on the bars a few times so the forks settle and slide freely on the axle. Then torque the axle nut to 115 N·m (85 lb-ft).
steps.title: Torque the axle nut

steps.instruction: Tighten the four axle pinch bolts to 21 N·m (15 lb-ft), going back and forth between the two bolts on each leg so the clamp closes evenly.
steps.title: Tighten the axle pinch bolts
verification: All four pinch bolts at 21 N·m (15 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Squeeze the front brake lever several times until it is firm, then spin the wheel. It should turn freely with only light pad drag and stop hard when you pull the lever.

verification: Wheel spins freely and brakes properly

steps.instruction: Turn the rebound and compression clickers in until they stop gently, then back out to your recorded positions. With the front wheel off the ground, take out the bleed screw on top of each fork leg to release the internal pressure, then refit it at 1.3 N·m (0.95 lb-ft).

verification: Pressure released, bleed screws at 1.3 N·m (0.95 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Off the stand, push the front down hard several times: the fork should move smoothly and quietly with no oil on the tubes. Recheck after the first ride for seal leaks.

steps.instruction: Check the damper for a bent rod or damage and its O-ring for wear. Check the base valve, its O-ring, bushing and spring and the bleed screw for wear or damage, clean the base valve if dirty, and check the upper spring seat face, the adjuster and its O-ring and the scraper. Replace anything worn.
steps.title: Inspect the damper and valves
verification: Damper, base valve, adjuster and seats inspected

steps.instruction: Wash all parts in clean solvent, blow them dry and lay them on clean rags. No grit or lint may get into the damper.
steps.title: Clean every part

steps.instruction: Pull the damper rod all the way out. Fill the damper with Yamaha Suspension Oil S1 until it is full. Pump the rod slowly up and down in strokes of about 200 mm to push the air out. Do not use longer strokes; that draws air back in, and if it happens start the fill again.
steps.title: Fill the damper
verification: Damper filled and bled with short strokes

steps.instruction: With the rod fully extended, measure from the top of the damper down to the oil and set it to 143–146 mm by adding or drawing off oil. Do the same on the other damper; both must match.
steps.title: Set the damper oil level
verification: Oil level 143–146 mm in both dampers

steps.instruction: Run the locknut fully down the damper rod by hand. Pull the damper rod out to full extension, then fit the base valve and let the rod come back as you screw it in. Check the damper is still fully extended; if not, repeat the fill and level steps. Hold the damper with the ring wrench and torque the base valve to 28 N·m (21 lb-ft), then fit the adjuster knob and its screw at 0.6 N·m (0.44 lb-ft).
steps.title: Refit the base valve

steps.instruction: Pump the damper rod slowly through its full travel more than 10 times to spread the oil. Then, with a cloth around the damper, push it fully in and hold it while the excess oil (about 10 cm³) runs out of the hole on the base valve end. Check the damper moves smoothly with no tight spots; if not, start again from the fill.
steps.title: Purge the excess oil

steps.instruction: Cover the end of the inner tube with a plastic bag wiped with fork oil so the seal lips are not cut. Slide on, in this order: new dust seal, scraper, stopper ring, new oil seal with its numbered side facing down toward the axle, washer, and the new outer tube bushing. Grease the dust seal and oil seal lips with lithium-soap grease and oil the inner tube.
steps.title: Load the new parts onto the inner tube
verification: Parts on in the right order

steps.instruction: Fit the new inner tube bushing (piston metal) into its slot at the top of the inner tube.
steps.title: Fit the new inner tube bushing

steps.instruction: Slide the outer tube onto the inner tube. Drive the outer tube bushing and washer into the outer tube with the fork seal driver until seated.
steps.title: Join the tubes and drive in the bushing

steps.instruction: Drive the new oil seal in with the fork seal driver until the stopper ring groove is completely visible above it, then fit the stopper ring fully into its groove.
steps.title: Drive in the oil seal and stopper ring

steps.instruction: Grease the inner tube, then press the scraper and new dust seal into the top of the outer tube. Slide the tubes through their stroke; they must move smoothly. If they bind, take them apart again and find out why.
steps.title: Fit the dust seal

steps.instruction: Measure from the bottom of the damper body to the bottom of the locknut on the rod. It must be 16 mm or more; turn the locknut to get it there.
steps.title: Check the locknut position on the damper rod

steps.instruction: Put the upper spring seat on with its larger diameter toward the spring, slide the spring onto the damper, and lower the damper slowly into the inner tube until it rests on the bottom. Do not let it drop; it can damage the tube.
steps.title: Fit the spring and damper
verification: Spring seat the right way round

steps.instruction: Turn the rebound clicker fully out (note where it was). Compress the inner tube and hold the damper rod out with the ring wrench between the tube and the locknut. Fit the damper adjusting rod (if fitted), a new copper washer and the adjuster, finger tight against the locknut. Measure the gap between adjuster and locknut: it must be 0.5–1.0 mm. Then hold the locknut and torque the adjuster to it at 29 N·m (21 lb-ft).
steps.title: Fit the adjuster to the damper rod
verification: Adjuster on the locknut at 29 N·m (21 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Put medium threadlocker on the adjuster threads, remove the ring wrench and screw the adjuster into the bottom of the inner tube. Torque it to 55 N·m (41 lb-ft).
steps.title: Screw the adjuster into the inner tube

steps.instruction: Fill the leg with 210 cm³ of Yamaha Suspension Oil S1. Use the same amount on both legs.
steps.title: Fill the outer chamber

steps.instruction: Screw the damper assembly (fork cap) into the outer tube by hand; it gets its final torque once the leg is in the clamps. Refit the protector guide.
steps.title: Refit the fork cap

steps.instruction: Slide each leg up through the clamps to the height you recorded (stock is 8 mm of tube above the top clamp). Snug the lower pinch bolts just enough to hold the leg.
steps.title: Put the legs back in the clamps
verification: Both legs at the same height (8 mm stock)

steps.instruction: Torque each damper assembly (fork cap) to 30 N·m (22 lb-ft) with the cap bolt ring wrench.
steps.title: Torque the fork caps

steps.instruction: Recheck the heights, then tighten the upper pinch bolts to 21 N·m (15 lb-ft) and the lower pinch bolts to 21 N·m (15 lb-ft). Do not overtighten the lower clamp; that squeezes the tube and makes the fork stick.
steps.title: Torque the clamp pinch bolts

steps.instruction: Refit the guards with the brake hose and any sensor lead in their guides and tighten the guard bolts to 5 N·m (3.7 lb-ft).
steps.title: Refit the fork guards

steps.instruction: Refit the headlight body (7 N·m (5.2 lb-ft)) and check the light works.
steps.title: Refit the headlight

steps.instruction: Unhook the caliper and bolt it back onto the left fork leg, torquing its two bolts to 28 N·m (21 lb-ft). Check the pads are still seated and spread enough for the disc.
steps.title: Bolt the caliper back on

steps.instruction: Grease the axle lightly with lithium-soap grease. Fit the collars to the hub on their own sides, lift the wheel into the forks with the disc sliding between the brake pads, and push the axle through from the side it came out.
steps.title: Lift the front wheel into the forks

steps.instruction: Put the speed sensor back on the left leg with its bracket, keeping the lead in its original routing. Tighten the bolt to 7 N·m (5.2 lb-ft). Check nothing magnetic or metallic is stuck to the sensor face.
steps.title: Refit the speed sensor

steps.instruction: Fit the axle nut and run it down. Before the final pull, take the bike off the stand or push hard on the bars a few times so the forks settle and slide freely on the axle. Then torque the axle nut to 115 N·m (85 lb-ft).
steps.title: Torque the axle nut

steps.instruction: Tighten the four axle pinch bolts to 21 N·m (15 lb-ft), going back and forth between the two bolts on each leg so the clamp closes evenly.
steps.title: Tighten the axle pinch bolts
verification: All four pinch bolts at 21 N·m (15 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Squeeze the front brake lever several times until it is firm, then spin the wheel. It should turn freely with only light pad drag and stop hard when you pull the lever.
steps.title: Pump up the front brake
verification: Wheel spins freely and brakes properly

steps.instruction: Turn the rebound and compression clickers in until they stop gently, then back out to your recorded positions. With the front wheel off the ground, take out the bleed screw on top of each fork leg to release the internal pressure, then refit it at 1.3 N·m (0.95 lb-ft).
steps.title: Restore clickers and bleed air
verification: Pressure released, bleed screws at 1.3 N·m (0.95 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Off the stand, push the front down hard several times: the fork should move smoothly and quietly with no oil on the tubes. Recheck after the first ride for seal leaks.
steps.title: Final check

title: Full fork service: seals, bushings, oil and damper bleed

completeness: Takes the shock out, removes the spring, inspects the shock body, renews the lower eye bearing and upper eye bushing with their seals, refits the spring at your recorded preload and reinstalls the shock with the linkage torqued; the nitrogen-charged damper is not opened, so damper oil, seals, valving and gas recharge are not covered.
critical_stop_conditions: Shock rod bent, scored or leaking oil or gas: the shock must be replaced or rebuilt by a suspension shop.
Never heat, puncture or clamp the damper body, and never try to open it: it holds high-pressure nitrogen.
Shock eye bore scored or out of round: stop, the shock body is damaged.
Spring cracked or worn through its coating at the guides: replace it.
Shock does not return fully or knocks after refit: do not ride.
entry_state: Complete bike, cold, on a stand under the engine with the rear wheel clear.
excluded: Damper internals: oil, seal head, piston, valving and nitrogen recharge (the damper is sealed and is not opened)
Linkage and swingarm needle bearings (see the linkage guide)
Changing to a different spring rate
exit_state: Shock refitted with inspected spring and new eye bearing/bushing and seals, preload restored, linkage torqued; ready to ride. Damper internals untouched.

required_parts.purpose: Fit new if worn; dust seals always new

required_parts.name: Shock upper eye bushing, stopper ring, O-rings and dust seals
required_parts.purpose: Fit new if worn; seals and O-rings always new

steps.instruction: Wash the bike, especially around the shock and linkage, and let it dry.
steps.title: Wash and prep

steps.instruction: Take off the seat, both side covers, both shrouds and the fuel tank so you can reach the top shock bolt. Bag each set of fasteners separately.
steps.title: Remove the seat, side covers, shrouds and tank

steps.instruction: Put the bike on a stand under the engine with the rear wheel clear. Support the swingarm with a block so it cannot drop when the shock comes out.
steps.title: Lift the rear wheel

steps.instruction: Count the rebound and both compression clicker positions back to the stop and write them down, then reset them. Measure the spring installed length (between the spring seats) and write it down so you can restore the same preload.
steps.title: Record shock settings and spring length

steps.instruction: Hold the swingarm and pull the shock lower bolt out of the relay arm.
steps.title: Remove the shock lower bolt

steps.instruction: Remove the upper bolt nut and bolt and lift the shock out downward and backward between the linkage and the frame. Keep it upright.
steps.title: Remove the shock upper bolt and shock

steps.instruction: Clamp the shock body lightly in a soft-jaw vise. Loosen the locknut, back the adjusting nut off until the spring is free, then remove the lower spring guide, upper spring guide and spring. Do not turn the shock shaft or touch the gas valve.
steps.title: Take the spring off

branches.condition: The lower eye bearing and the upper eye bushing turn smoothly with no play, and the seals are only going to be cleaned and regreased.
branches.label: Eye bearing and bushing are good

steps.instruction: Wipe the shaft and look for bends, scoring or any oil or gas leak. Check the spring and spring guides for cracks and wear, and the bolts for bends or wear. A leaking or worn damper goes to a suspension shop for a damper rebuild, or the shock assembly is replaced; never open it yourself. Note what you find.
steps.title: Inspect the shock and spring

steps.instruction: Pull the collars and dust seals out of both shock eyes. Feel the lower needle bearing and the upper bushing for play, roughness or rust. Replace whatever is worn.
steps.title: Check the eye bearing and bushing
verification: Eye bearing and bushing condition noted

steps.instruction: Press the old needle bearing out of the lower eye. Press the new one in by its outer race until it sits 4.25 mm below each face of the eye (measure with a depth gauge). Grease the needles with molybdenum disulfide grease, but keep grease off the outer race and the eye bore. Fit the bushing and collars and new dust seals, lips pointing in toward the bearing.
steps.title: Renew the lower eye bearing
verification: New bearing at 4.25 mm installed depth

steps.instruction: Press the new upper bushing into the shock eye squarely until the stopper ring groove shows, fit the stopper ring, then push the bushing back until it sits against the ring. Grease the new O-rings with lithium-soap grease and fit the collars and new dust seals.
steps.title: Renew the upper eye bushing
verification: Bushing in and stopper ring seated

steps.instruction: Fit the spring, upper guide and lower guide. Turn the adjusting nut down until the spring installed length matches what you recorded and lock it with the locknut (10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft)). Measure the length again.
steps.title: Refit the spring
verification: Spring length matches the recorded value

steps.instruction: Coat the shock upper and lower bolts and the lower eye bearing and seals with molybdenum disulfide grease.
steps.title: Grease the shock bolts and eyes

steps.instruction: Lift the swingarm, guide the shock up into place and push the upper bolt in from the right side and the lower bolt in from the left. Fit the nuts finger tight.
steps.title: Fit the shock
verification: Upper bolt from the right, lower bolt from the left

steps.instruction: Torque the shock upper nut to 56 N·m (41 lb-ft) and the shock lower nut to 53 N·m (39 lb-ft). While you are there, check the linkage nuts: connecting arm at the frame 80 N·m (59 lb-ft), connecting arm at the relay arm 80 N·m (59 lb-ft), relay arm at the swingarm 70 N·m (52 lb-ft).
steps.title: Torque the shock and linkage
verification: Shock upper nut at 56 N·m (41 lb-ft)
Shock lower nut at 53 N·m (39 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Refit the fuel tank, shrouds, side covers and seat, checking the fuel line and breather hoses are not pinched.
steps.title: Refit the tank and bodywork
verification: Tank and bodywork on, hoses free

steps.instruction: Set the clickers back to your recorded positions. Off the stand, bounce the rear several times and check it moves smoothly. Check rider sag before riding. Give the shock about 50 km of easy riding to bed in.
steps.title: Restore settings and check sag

O-rings on the base valve and adjuster

Cap bolt wrench for the base valve

Yamaha Suspension Oil S1 fork oil

Flat-blade screwdriver (wrapped) for the stopper ring

steps.instruction: Wash the bike, especially the fork tubes and clamps, and set up a clean bench with lint-free rags. Dirt inside this fork is the main cause of short seal and damper life.
steps.title: Wash and prep

steps.instruction: Write down the compression and rebound clicker positions (count in to the stop, then return) and how far the fork tubes stand above the top clamp on each side.
steps.title: Record settings and height

steps.instruction: Put the bike on a stand under the engine with the front wheel clear and check it is stable.
steps.title: Lift the front wheel

steps.instruction: Undo the speed sensor bracket bolt on the left fork leg and lift the sensor away from the wheel without pulling on its lead. Tape it to the fork guard so it hangs clear. Keep magnetic tools away from the sensor and its rotor on the wheel.
steps.title: Unbolt the speed sensor
verification: Sensor hanging free, lead not stretched

steps.instruction: Loosen the four axle pinch bolts at the bottom of both fork legs, then crack the axle nut loose. Do not take anything off yet; the wheel is still holding the forks in line.
steps.title: Loosen the axle
verification: Pinch bolts and axle nut loose

steps.instruction: Hold the wheel, unscrew the axle nut and slide the axle out. Lower the wheel out of the forks and lay it with the disc facing up. Pick up the two collars from the hub and keep them with the axle so they go back on the correct sides.
steps.title: Pull the front wheel
verification: Wheel out, axle and both collars bagged together

steps.instruction: Remove the two caliper bolts, slide the caliper off the disc and hang it from the frame with a strap so the hose is not stretched. Do not pull the brake lever while it is off.
steps.title: Unbolt and hang the caliper

steps.instruction: Take the headlight body off so you can reach the top of the fork legs, leaving it hanging on its wiring with no strain.
steps.title: Move the headlight out of the way
verification: Headlight clear of the fork caps

steps.instruction: Undo the fork guard (protector) bolts on each leg and take the guards off, freeing the brake hose and any sensor lead from their guides.
steps.title: Remove the fork guards

steps.instruction: Loosen the upper clamp pinch bolts on one leg. With the leg still held by the lower clamp, crack the damper assembly (fork cap) loose with the cap bolt ring wrench. Repeat on the other leg.
steps.title: Loosen the fork caps in the clamps

steps.instruction: Hold each leg, loosen its lower clamp pinch bolts and slide it down out of the clamps. Label them left and right.
steps.title: Pull both legs

steps.instruction: Clamp the leg upright in a soft-jaw vise by the axle bracket, unscrew the damper assembly from the outer tube, and pump the outer tube to drain the oil into a pan. Look at the oil: metal flakes or a grey colour mean worn bushings.
steps.title: Unscrew the cap and drain the outer oil

steps.instruction: Compress the inner tube and slip the cap bolt ring wrench in between the inner tube and the damper locknut so the damper rod is held out. Hold the locknut and unscrew the adjuster at the bottom of the leg. Leave the locknut where it is: if you remove it the damper rod can drop inside the damper and is hard to recover. Pull out the damper adjusting rod (if fitted), then the damper with its spring and spring seat.
steps.title: Remove the bottom adjuster
verification: Adjuster off, locknut still on the rod

steps.instruction: Pry the dust seal up out of the outer tube, then lift the stopper ring out of its groove with a wrapped flat screwdriver. Do not scratch the inner tube.
steps.title: Remove the dust seal and stopper ring
verification: Dust seal and stopper ring out

steps.instruction: Push the inner tube in slowly until it is just short of bottoming, then pull it out sharply. Repeat until the bushings knock the oil seal out and the tubes come apart. Slide the old seal, washer and bushings off the inner tube.
steps.title: Separate the tubes

steps.instruction: Note the compression clicker position and turn it fully out. Hold the damper with the cap bolt ring wrench and unscrew the base valve with the cap bolt wrench. Drain the damper oil.
steps.title: Remove the base valve from the damper

steps.instruction: Check the inner tube chrome for scratches and the oil lock piece for damage; light marks can be polished with 1000-grit wet paper. Roll the tube in V-blocks under a dial gauge: the bend is half the gauge swing and must not exceed 0.2 mm. Check the outer tube bore for wear or scoring. Record the bend reading.
steps.title: Inspect the tubes
verification: Inner tube bend at or under 0.2 mm

steps.instruction: Measure the fork spring free length. Under 492.0 mm it must be replaced.
steps.title: Measure the spring

steps.instruction: Check the damper for a bent rod or damage and its O-ring for wear. Check the base valve, its O-ring, bushing and spring and the bleed screw for wear or damage, clean the base valve if dirty, and check the upper spring seat face, the adjuster and its O-ring. Replace anything worn.
steps.title: Inspect the damper and valves
verification: Damper, base valve, adjuster and seats inspected

steps.instruction: Wash all parts in clean solvent, blow them dry and lay them on clean rags. No grit or lint may get into the damper.
steps.title: Clean every part

steps.instruction: Pull the damper rod all the way out. Fill the damper with Yamaha Suspension Oil S1 (216 cm³). Pump the rod slowly up and down in strokes of about 200 mm to push the air out. Do not use longer strokes; that draws air back in, and if it happens start the fill again.
steps.title: Fill the damper
verification: Damper filled and bled with short strokes

steps.instruction: With the rod fully extended, measure from the top of the damper down to the oil and set it to 145–148 mm by adding or drawing off oil. Do the same on the other damper; both must match.
steps.title: Set the damper oil level
verification: Oil level 145–148 mm in both dampers

steps.instruction: Run the locknut fully down the damper rod by hand. Pull the damper rod out to full extension, then fit the base valve and let the rod come back as you screw it in. Check the damper is still fully extended; if not, repeat the fill and level steps. Hold the damper with the ring wrench and torque the base valve to 28 N·m (21 lb-ft).
steps.title: Refit the base valve

steps.instruction: Pump the damper rod slowly through its full travel more than 10 times to spread the oil. Then, with a cloth around the damper, push it fully in and hold it while the excess oil (about 10 cm³) runs out of the hole on the base valve end. Check the damper moves smoothly with no tight spots; if not, start again from the fill.
steps.title: Purge the excess oil

steps.instruction: Cover the end of the inner tube with a plastic bag wiped with fork oil so the seal lips are not cut. Slide on, in this order: new dust seal, stopper ring, new oil seal with its numbered side facing down toward the axle, washer, and the new outer tube bushing. Grease the dust seal and oil seal lips with lithium-soap grease and oil the inner tube.
steps.title: Load the new parts onto the inner tube
verification: Parts on in the right order

steps.instruction: Fit the new inner tube bushing (piston metal) into its slot at the top of the inner tube.
steps.title: Fit the new inner tube bushing

steps.instruction: Grease the inner tube, then press the new dust seal into the top of the outer tube. Slide the tubes through their stroke; they must move smoothly. If they bind, take them apart again and find out why.

steps.instruction: Measure from the bottom of the damper body to the bottom of the locknut on the rod. It must be 16 mm or more; turn the locknut to get it there.
steps.title: Check the locknut position on the damper rod

steps.instruction: Put the upper spring seat on with its larger diameter toward the spring, slide the spring onto the damper, and lower the damper slowly into the inner tube until it rests on the bottom. Do not let it drop; it can damage the tube.
steps.title: Fit the spring and damper
verification: Spring seat the right way round

steps.instruction: Turn the rebound clicker fully out (note where it was). Compress the inner tube and hold the damper rod out with the ring wrench between the tube and the locknut. Fit the damper adjusting rod (if fitted), a new copper washer and the adjuster, finger tight against the locknut. Measure the gap between adjuster and locknut: it must be 0.5–1.0 mm. Then hold the locknut and torque the adjuster to it at 29 N·m (21 lb-ft).
steps.title: Fit the adjuster to the damper rod
verification: Adjuster on the locknut at 29 N·m (21 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Put medium threadlocker on the adjuster threads, remove the ring wrench and screw the adjuster into the bottom of the inner tube. Torque it to 55 N·m (41 lb-ft).
steps.title: Screw the adjuster into the inner tube

steps.instruction: Fill the leg with 290 cm³ of Yamaha Suspension Oil S1 (the adjustment range is 260–365 cm³). Use the same amount on both legs.
steps.title: Fill the outer chamber

steps.instruction: Screw the damper assembly (fork cap) into the outer tube by hand; it gets its final torque once the leg is in the clamps. Refit the protector guide.
steps.title: Refit the fork cap

steps.instruction: Slide each leg up through the clamps to the height you recorded (stock is 5 mm of tube above the top clamp). Snug the lower pinch bolts just enough to hold the leg.
steps.title: Put the legs back in the clamps
verification: Both legs at the same height (5 mm stock)

steps.instruction: Torque each damper assembly (fork cap) to 30 N·m (22 lb-ft) with the cap bolt ring wrench.
steps.title: Torque the fork caps

steps.instruction: Recheck the heights, then tighten the upper pinch bolts to 21 N·m (15 lb-ft) and the lower pinch bolts to 21 N·m (15 lb-ft). Do not overtighten the lower clamp; that squeezes the tube and makes the fork stick.
steps.title: Torque the clamp pinch bolts

steps.instruction: Refit the guards with the brake hose and any sensor lead in their guides and tighten the guard bolts to 5 N·m (3.7 lb-ft).
steps.title: Refit the fork guards

steps.instruction: Refit the headlight body (7 N·m (5.2 lb-ft)) and check the light works.
steps.title: Refit the headlight

steps.instruction: Unhook the caliper and bolt it back onto the left fork leg, torquing its two bolts to 28 N·m (21 lb-ft). Check the pads are still seated and spread enough for the disc.
steps.title: Bolt the caliper back on

steps.instruction: Grease the axle lightly with lithium-soap grease. Fit the collars to the hub on their own sides, lift the wheel into the forks with the disc sliding between the brake pads, and push the axle through from the side it came out.

steps.instruction: Put the speed sensor back on the left leg with its bracket, keeping the lead in its original routing. Tighten the bolt to 7 N·m (5.2 lb-ft). Check nothing magnetic or metallic is stuck to the sensor face.
steps.title: Refit the speed sensor

steps.instruction: Fit the axle nut and run it down. Before the final pull, take the bike off the stand or push hard on the bars a few times so the forks settle and slide freely on the axle. Then torque the axle nut to 115 N·m (85 lb-ft).
steps.title: Torque the axle nut

steps.instruction: Tighten the four axle pinch bolts to 21 N·m (15 lb-ft), going back and forth between the two bolts on each leg so the clamp closes evenly.
steps.title: Tighten the axle pinch bolts
verification: All four pinch bolts at 21 N·m (15 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Squeeze the front brake lever several times until it is firm, then spin the wheel. It should turn freely with only light pad drag and stop hard when you pull the lever.
steps.title: Pump up the front brake
verification: Wheel spins freely and brakes properly

steps.instruction: Turn the rebound and compression clickers in until they stop gently, then back out to your recorded positions. With the front wheel off the ground, take out the bleed screw on top of each fork leg to release the internal pressure, then refit it at 1.3 N·m (0.95 lb-ft).

verification: Pressure released, bleed screws at 1.3 N·m (0.95 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Off the stand, push the front down hard several times: the fork should move smoothly and quietly with no oil on the tubes. Recheck after the first ride for seal leaks.

steps.instruction: Pull the collars and dust seals out of both shock eyes. Feel the lower needle bearing and the upper bushing for play, roughness or rust. Replace whatever is worn.

steps.instruction: Press the old needle bearing out of the lower eye. Press the new one in by its outer race until it sits 4.25 mm below each face of the eye (measure with a depth gauge). steps.instruction: Press the new upper bushing into the shock eye squarely until the stopper ring groove shows, fit the stopper ring, then push the bushing back until it sits against the ring. Grease the new O-rings with lithium-soap grease and fit the collars and new dust seals.

steps.instruction: Fit the spring, upper guide and lower guide. Turn the adjusting nut down until the spring installed length matches what you recorded and lock it with the locknut (10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft)). Measure the length again.

steps.instruction: Coat the shock upper and lower bolts and the lower eye bearing and seals with molybdenum disulfide grease.

completeness: Takes the shock out, removes the spring, inspects the shock body, renews the lower eye bearing and upper eye bushing with their seals, refits the spring at your recorded preload and reinstalls the shock with the linkage torqued; the nitrogen-charged damper is not opened, so damper oil, seals, valving and gas recharge are not covered.
critical_stop_conditions: Shock rod bent, scored or leaking oil or gas: the shock must be replaced or rebuilt by a suspension shop.
Never heat, puncture or clamp the damper body, and never try to open it: it holds high-pressure nitrogen.
Shock eye bore scored or out of round: stop, the shock body is damaged.
Spring cracked or worn through its coating at the guides: replace it.
Shock does not return fully or knocks after refit: do not ride.
entry_state: Complete bike, cold, on a stand under the engine with the rear wheel clear.
excluded: Damper internals: oil, seal head, piston, valving and nitrogen recharge (the damper is sealed and is not opened)

Changing to a different spring rate
exit_state: Shock refitted with inspected spring and new eye bearing/bushing and seals, preload restored, linkage torqued; ready to ride. Damper internals untouched.
prerequisites: Bike washed; seat, side covers, shrouds and fuel tank off for access to the top shock bolt.
